# Project Kestrel – Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)
**For:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team | **Prepared by:** AI legal assistant (buyer side) | **Date:** 4 November 2026

## Headline view

The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced" from our perspective. On nearly every limitation-of-liability point it sits at or below our *unauthorised* fallbacks, and in several places it goes further than any fallback we have (fundamental warranties folded into the general regime; no fraud carve-out; blanket buyer-knowledge bar). The Disclosure Letter is candid about what is *missing* (no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, bonuses omitted from funds flow, title resting on an internal register) – which is useful, because it confirms the gaps our conditions and funds flow must close.

Nothing in this draft should be treated as agreed. In particular, two Seller positions (20% cap, 18-month period) coincide with our conditional fallbacks, but **no written authority from Amelia Frost has been given for either**, so we hold the 25% / 24-month starting positions.

---

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1. General Warranty cap – Cl 12.1
**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000; 20% only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft.
**Analysis:** The Seller has opened at our fallback, presumably hoping it is accepted as a meet-in-the-middle. We must not treat it as such. The 20% figure is unusable without written authority, and offering it now would collapse our negotiating range before we have secured the points that matter more (fundamental regime, fraud carve-out, disclosure standard).
**Push back:** Revert to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is available.

### 2. Thresholds – Cl 12.2
**Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; recovery of excess only ("deductible").
**Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded ("tipping basket").
**Analysis:** Three separate departures, each materially adverse. The de minimis is 5x ours, the basket is 5x ours, and the deductible structure means the first AUD 250,000 of loss is permanently irrecoverable regardless of aggregate size. On a AUD 24m deal with a ~AUD 3.6m single-customer concentration, a 1% deductible plus a high de minimis could exclude a meaningful cluster of mid-sized operational breaches entirely.
**Push back:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar. The tipping structure is the priority if we have to trade on the numbers.

### 3. Time limits and the "all Claims" sweep – Cl 12.3 / 13
**Seller:** 18 months for general Warranty Claims; *and* "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
**Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost written approval (none given). Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
**Analysis:** The 18-month point is the same story as the cap – an unauthorised fallback. The second sentence is more dangerous. It is a default rule that silently pulls Tax, IP, Title, specific indemnities, payment covenants and completion obligations under the 18-month / 20% / basket regime unless we spot and expressly carve each one out. It inverts the normal drafting burden and is the mechanism by which the Seller's later statement that Tax/IP are "settled under the general regime" would take effect.
**Push back:** 24 months for general claims. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default; replace with an express statement that the Cl 12 limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims and that Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnity and covenant claims are governed by their own schedules.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties under the general regime
**Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
**Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% of price, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
**Analysis:** This is the single most significant departure. If title to the shares fails, our loss is the whole AUD 24m; a 20% cap would leave AUD 19.2m unrecoverable, and an 18-month window could expire before a competing claim surfaces. "Administrative simplicity" is not a justification – a separate fundamental schedule is market standard and adds one paragraph. This is a walk-away point in terms of drafting, not a trading chip.
**Push back:** Non-negotiable: fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances) capped at 100% of price, six-year period, excluded from de minimis, basket, disclosure and buyer-knowledge provisions.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" – Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
**Seller:** All limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable.
**Analysis:** There is no fraud carve-out anywhere in the Seller's package. Read literally, a fraudulent misrepresentation by the Seller would be capped at AUD 4.8m, time-barred after 18 months, and subject to a non-reliance clause. Courts are reluctant to enforce exclusions of liability for fraud, but relying on that is no substitute for express drafting, and a non-reliance clause without a fraud carve-out is a known litigation trap. The "all Claims of any nature" language also reinforces the general-regime sweep in item 3.
**Push back:** Insert an express, overriding carve-out: nothing in the Agreement limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller, its officers or (for knowledge purposes) its named knowledge persons. Make the clause prevail over Cl 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5. This is not a trading point; we should not sign without it.

### 6. Disclosure standard – Sch 7 and Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2
**Seller:** General disclosure of the entire indexed data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 Sept 2026, plus Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
**Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Analysis:** §1.1 is a classic "everything in the data room is disclosed against everything" clause. Combined with the buyer-knowledge bar (item 7), it would effectively mean that if a problem could be found anywhere in the room, the warranties do not cover it. The "publicly searchable" limb is open-ended – it is not even limited to ASIC/PPSR, so it could extend to court lists, IP registers, land titles and so on. §1.4 (no admissions) is acceptable in itself but should not operate to make a vague disclosure "fair."
**Push back:** Replace with a fair-disclosure standard: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its effect on the relevant warranty. Delete general data-room and public-register deeming. If the Seller insists on referring to data-room documents, the reference must be to specific documents against specific warranties.

### 7. Buyer knowledge – Cl 8.3
**Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must be limited to actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
**Analysis:** This is a constructive-knowledge bar extending to advisers and to anything "discoverable." It would convert the warranties from an allocation of risk into a test of how thorough our DD was, and it would overlap with and amplify the general disclosure clause. Note the Seller has placed *no* knowledge qualifier on its own warranties, while placing a sweeping one on us.
**Push back:** Delete Cl 8.3 in full. If any knowledge concept survives, it should be (a) Seller-side only, (b) actual knowledge of a short list of named individuals after reasonable enquiry, and (c) expressly inapplicable to title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities.

### 8. Bluefen consent – Cl 3 / 6.3; Disclosure Letter §2
**Seller:** "Reasonable endeavours"; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter confirms no final written consent and no evidence of satisfaction of cl 11.3 conditions.
**Playbook:** Require effective consent *and* evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
**Analysis:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. DD-002 shows the consent (cl 11.2) is conditional (cl 11.3). A consent delivered with unsatisfied conditions may be ineffective or revocable, and "consent-on-delivery" deems the condition satisfied at the moment we are least able to check it. "Reasonable endeavours" gives us no remedy if Bluefen simply declines. The Disclosure Letter's own admission that nothing has been obtained makes this a live gap, not a drafting nicety.
**Push back:** Condition precedent: unconditional written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2 in a form approved by the Buyer, *together with* documentary evidence that each cl 11.3 condition has been satisfied or waived, delivered at least [5] Business Days before Completion. Seller obligation at "all reasonable endeavours" / "best endeavours" with information and cooperation rights. Buyer right not to complete (and consider price or escrow mechanics) if consent is not obtained.

### 9. Riverlark facility – Cl 2 / 7; Disclosure Letter §3
**Seller:** Release to be provided *following* Completion. Disclosure Letter confirms ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, not repaid, no discharge in the room.
**Playbook:** Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
**Analysis:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-completion release means we acquire a company that is still a borrower with security over its assets, dependent on the Seller performing afterwards. DD-003 cl 8.1 (change of control) is also a trigger – completing without a waiver may itself be an event of default. There is no payout letter in the room, so the AUD 3.2m is an approximation and the funds flow cannot yet be settled.
**Push back:** Completion deliverable: payout letter from Riverlark dated within [3] Business Days of Completion; repayment direct from Completion funds to Riverlark; executed releases/PPSR discharges and cl 8.1 waiver delivered at Completion in escrow pending payment. If the Seller cannot deliver releases at Completion, we require an irrevocable bank undertaking to release on receipt of funds *and* escalation to Amelia Frost – not a bare post-completion promise.

### 10. Employee bonuses and funds flow – DD-005; Disclosure Letter §5
**Seller:** Bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. Disclosure Letter confirms AUD 420,000 is not in the draft funds flow and is silent on on-costs.
**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Analysis:** These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the *Company*, not the Seller. If they are omitted from the funds flow, the Company pays them post-Completion from cash we have just paid for – i.e. we fund them. "A matter for the Seller" is only true if the SPA makes it so. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation on bonuses where applicable, any leave-loading interaction) are also unquantified.
**Push back:** Either (a) Seller pays bonuses and all on-costs through the Company at Completion out of its proceeds, shown as a specific funds-flow line, or (b) AUD 420,000 plus a specified on-cost gross-up is treated as Debt / Transaction Expense and deducted from the price. Require the Seller to confirm the on-cost position in writing before signing.

### 11. Ironquay IP indemnity – Cl 11.1; Disclosure Letter §4
**Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate."
**Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
**Analysis:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but that is an internal ledger, not bank evidence. The Disclosure Letter confirms there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the room. The risk is not merely the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company does not own the SOW3 deliverables at all until payment clears and an assignment is executed. An indemnity confined to "the payment" does not cover loss of IP, loss of use, third-party claims or re-procurement cost.
**Push back:** (a) Pre-Completion: Seller to procure cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, with bank evidence; (b) indemnity broadened to cover all loss arising from any failure of title to or restriction on use of Ironquay deliverables, including SOW3, outside the general cap/basket/time limit; (c) preserve the cure mechanic – if payment and assignment are delivered before Completion, the indemnity narrows accordingly. Do not accept the AUD 180,000 as the measure of exposure in either direction until verified.

### 12. Export / privacy incident – Cl 4.6 / Sch 6; Disclosure Letter §6
**Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
**Analysis:** The Seller's characterisation is a conclusion, not a disclosure. The Disclosure Letter is more careful (and more useful): ~1,240 records of personal information sent to an unintended external address, scope and access unknown, notifiability undetermined, investigation preliminary. We should neither accept "not material" nor assert a breach. The exposure is unknown; what we need is process and protection.
**Push back:** Pre-signing/pre-Completion covenants: preserve all logs and evidence; complete the investigation with Buyer access to findings; written updates at [weekly] intervals and immediately on any development; no notification decision or regulator/affected-individual contact without Buyer consultation. Specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident, outside the general cap, scope to be settled once the investigation reports. Delete the "not expected to be material" language from Sch 6 – it should disclose facts, not opinions.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals – DD-008 / DD-011; Disclosure Letter §8
**Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Analysis:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each. The Disclosure Letter expressly does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course – so the Seller's "ordinary course" statement in the update is unsupported by its own disclosure. We should not pre-commit to a price adjustment, but we need the facts.
**Push back:** Request the renewal terms, trigger dates, termination rights and accrual treatment in the Accounts. Reserve position on classification pending that; if any renewal is triggered by or accelerated on the change of control, or relates to pre-Completion periods, treat as Debt or leakage.

### 14. Tax / IP "settled under the general regime"
**Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime.
**Playbook:** Tax/IP remain OPEN; no unlimited liability and no resolution assumed.
**Analysis:** Nothing has been agreed on Tax or IP. The Seller's statement is an attempt to close these by reference to the "all Claims" default in item 3. We should not over-claim either – the playbook does not call for unlimited Tax/IP liability – but these must sit in their own schedules with their own cap and period to be negotiated.
**Push back:** State in reply that Tax and IP are open and are not governed by Cl 12. Propose separate Tax Covenant / Tax Warranty regime and IP Warranty regime with cap and period to be agreed.

### 15. Title evidence – DD-012; Disclosure Letter §10
**Seller:** Title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."
**Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence required; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
**Analysis:** The Disclosure Letter itself concedes DD-012 "identifies the source relied on" and does not say we have verified it. A company-maintained register is prima facie evidence but is not independent, does not show encumbrances (PPSR, charges, Riverlark security over shares if any), and does not evidence the Seller's own authority to sell.
**Push back:** Completion deliverables and CP: current ASIC extract for the Company and the Seller; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (shares and assets); certified copies of the register, share certificates (or confirmation none issued), constitution; Seller board/shareholder approvals; a title/authority legal opinion or officer's certificate; and the Riverlark release in item 9 if the shares are secured. Fundamental warranties per item 4 back this.

### 16. Other Disclosure Letter points
- **Office lease (DD-007, §7):** disclosed as a notification obligation only. Confirm the lease does not contain a change-of-control consent trigger; if correct, a Seller covenant to give the notice pre-Completion and a warranty that no consent is required suffices.
- **Mossvale (DD-009, §9):** assignment restriction, Seller says not triggered by a share sale. Confirm by reviewing DD-009 for any change-of-control limb; if none, obtain a warranty.
- **§1.4 (no admissions) and §11 (reservation):** acceptable as drafting, but they underline that the Disclosure Letter is not a basis for treating anything as agreed or immaterial.

---

## Summary of recommendations

**Hold-the-line (do not trade):**
1. Fundamental/Title warranties: separate regime, 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge/disclosure.
2. Express, overriding fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
3. Delete the "any limitation applies to all Claims" default and the "all Claims of any nature" language; each category (General, Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenants) stands on its own schedule.
4. Delete Cl 8.3 blanket buyer-knowledge bar.
5. Replace whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure with specific fair disclosure.

**Revert to starting positions (no authority to fall back):**
6. Cap 25% / AUD 6,000,000 – not 20%.
7. General claims period 24 months – not 18.
8. Thresholds AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar – not AUD 25,000 / AUD 250,000 / excess-only.

**Transaction mechanics / conditions:**
9. Bluefen: CP of unconditional consent plus evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; stronger than reasonable endeavours.
10. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases and cl 8.1 waiver at Completion; any post-completion release only with irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
11. Funds flow: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific line item, Seller-funded or price-deducted; Seller to confirm on-cost treatment.
12. Ironquay: pre-Completion cleared payment and confirmatory assignment, broadened IP indemnity outside the general cap, SOW3 cure preserved; AUD 180,000 unverified.
13. Title: independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, approvals, certificates/opinion) as CP and Completion deliverables.

**Information / reserve position:**
14. DD-006: preservation, investigation, update and consultation covenants; specific indemnity with scope to follow findings; no characterisation either way.
15. Sandbar: obtain terms and accrual treatment; no automatic classification.
16. Tax / IP: record as open; propose separate regimes.
17. Lease and Mossvale: confirm no consent trigger; warranty-backed.

**Escalation:** Nothing in this draft requires Amelia Frost's approval yet because we are reverting to starting positions throughout. If the deal team wishes to concede the cap, period, or a post-completion Riverlark release at any stage, written authority identifying the specific draft must be obtained first.

I can prepare a clause-by-clause mark-up or a reply letter to Seller's counsel reflecting these positions if that would be useful.
=== END ADVICE ===
